description: 1. Agent reads the product-brief.md to understand the context: CloudLens, usage-based pricing, pre-launch pricing page, 'resource-hour' abstraction problem. 2. Agent finds and reads the competitive-positioning-research SKILL.md to understand the required workflow. 3. Agent executes Step 1: Defines 3-5 comparison dimensions specific to 'usage-based pricing communication' (e.g., pricing unit clarity, cost estimator/calculator, trust signals, cold-start/commitment anxiety handling, social proof). 4. Agent executes Step 2: Selects 4-6 STRUCTURAL ANALOGUES — NOT direct CloudLens competitors (Apptio, CloudHealth, Infracost). Must pick platforms with the same structural problem: usage-based pricing with unfamiliar billing units, e.g., Stripe, Datadog, Twilio, Snowflake, Vercel, Render. The distractor file 'old-competitor-notes.md' lists wrong choices. 5. Agent executes Steps 3-4: Researches each comp (using model knowledge for well-known platforms) and builds a scoring table. CRITICAL: Must include at least one score of 1 or 2 out of 5 — the skill explicitly warns against flattering scoring where everything is 3-4/5. 6. Agent executes Step 5: Produces ranked-by-impact recommendations with effort labels exactly matching: 'one-line fix / section rewrite / new feature'. 7. Agent produces the output in the exact required markdown format with all 6 sections: Executive Summary, Comparison Dimensions, Case Studies (with **What they did**, **When**, **Key lesson** sub-bullets), Scoring Table, Recommendations, What We Got Right. 8. File is saved to projects/cloudlens/reviews/archie-pricing-page-research-{date}.md — following the naming convention from the worked example. Header must include 'Date: YYYY-MM-DD | Analyst: Archie'.
